todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: A 30.5 inch high over the Plains slides south of the Great Lakes today before building to 30.6 inches over the Mid-Atlantic Sunday morning. This high shifts east into the Canadian Maritimes into Sunday night while a 29.1 inch low moves from Manitoba to Hudson Bay. This low will bring a 30.0 inch through across western Lake Superior Sunday afternoon. High pressure ridging of 30.3 inches returns to the Upper Great Lakes by Monday. This builds to 30.4 inches over Lake Superior Monday night and continues building to 30.5 inches Tuesday morning over northern Quebec. Ridging over Lake Superior will weaken into Wednesday. A 30.1 inch trough will move through Lake Superior Wednesday night.

marineWeather.synopsis: Low pressure around 29.4 inches has moved well east of the region, as strong high pressure around 30.6 inches remains over the Central Plains but begins to nudge in. Scattered showers will linger this morning over the southern half of Lake Michigan. A few rumbles of thunder and some isolated waterspout potential will remain over the south half of Lake Michigan. As the high shifts toward the Ohio River Valley today, strong low pressure around 29.0 inches will develop in south central Canada, shifting toward and into Hudson Bay on Sunday. This will likely bring southwest gales to far northern portions of Lake Michigan tonight into Sunday night. Gale Warning is now in effect from 9z Sunday until 6z Monday for the northern third of Lake Michigan. High pressure around 30.5 inches should develop east northeast of the region next week, bringing dry conditions and light to modest winds.

marineWeather.synopsis: A ridge of high pressure passes across the central Great Lakes this morning then settles across the Ohio Valley on Sunday. This produces gusty westerly winds on Sunday as deep low pressure tracks across northern Ontario. The high pressure then builds northward into the Great Lakes early next week.
High pressure 30.50 inches will build into the region today, weakening slightly to 30.30 inches by mid to late next week.

A 29.1 inch low over the Canadian Maritimes today will move northeast and into the North Atlantic by this evening. A 30.5 inch high will then build into the Ohio Valley tonight, expanding into the Mid Atlantic and New England Sunday through Monday while gradually weakening to 30.3 inches. Another 30.4 inch high will then build east across Quebec Tuesday through Wednesday.
